10-add-a-random-batch-to-the-person-judg.line: Still first: idea 5 judged no random batch, so nobody knows how far any method sits above chance.

why.impact: Without a chance rate, idea 5's 83% against 96% on hand cannot say whether either source finds anything a random pick would not.
why.odds: Adding a random batch to a review is easy and almost certain to give a usable baseline.
why.path: Nothing waits on it now; it is the missing control for idea 5's result.

9-a-stronger-picture-embedding-for-tags-.line: Lower: it would be measured on held-out verdicts, which idea 5 showed do not predict what a person confirms in the library.

why.impact: It would open fine-grained tags, but those are mostly the anomaly tagger's own, and any offline win now needs a human check.
why.odds: Idea 1's DINOv3 probe did well on defect tags, but with about 1,200 labels rather than 100.

12-have-a-person-judge-the-vote-s-top-10.line: Settles idea 3's open verdict; slightly more relevant now that the shipped vote is the source to beat.

why.impact: It decides which version of the shipped vote is the baseline, which matters more now that the vote held its own in idea 5.
why.odds: The two lists differ only where the old 55% bar lets fewer than 100 through, so a difference is likely only on the rarest tags.
why.path: Nothing waits on it; could share a short judging game with idea 10.

15-have-a-person-judge-the-unjudged-pict.line: Largely answered by idea 5, which judged only never-judged pictures: the classifier's top 100 was 83% right on hand and 53% on jewelry.

why.impact: Idea 5 already shows the never-judged picks are mostly right on hand, so held-out tests did not understate the classifier against the shipped vote; only the optional with-and-without-background comparison is new.
why.odds: Counting confirms in a judged list is straightforward.
why.path: Nothing waits on it; a candidate for closing from idea 5's report, or for riding along in idea 10's judging.

7-combine-the-classifier-and-the-near-ne.line: Weak: the lists barely overlap (2 to 20 shared pictures), but combining a weaker classifier with a stronger vote is unlikely to beat the vote.

why.impact: If the classifier does not beat the vote, a combination is unlikely to ship.
why.odds: Idea 5 found the classifier clearly behind on hand and not clearly ahead on jewelry.

11-use-the-base-rate-thresholds-as-the-n.line: Already answered in practice: ideas 4 and 5 ran the shipped near-neighbour kernel copied unchanged.

why.odds: Using the shipped code is what ideas 4 and 5 did.
why.path: Nothing waits on it; a candidate for closing.

8-pick-the-next-pictures-to-judge-by-the.line: Last: it speeds up a classifier that idea 5 found no better than the shipped vote, and idea 2 found such rankings no better than random.

why.impact: It saves verdicts but does not answer whether the classifier works.
why.odds: Idea 2 concluded negative, and idea 5 came back negative.
why.path: Idea 5 is concluded negative, so nothing it could speed up has been shown to work.
